To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a fully digital inductive buck regulator with a multi-sampled compensator and a lightweight auto-tuner.

a fully integrated inductive regulator with an all-digital control loop, a multi-sampled compensation scheme, and a lightweight auto-tuner can achieve a peak efficiency of over 90% and a 3.5-V/ $\mu s$  output slew during reference transient.
we propose a 125-MHz inductive buck regulator in 130-nM CMOS with 11.6 nH wire bond inductance and on-chip 3.2 nF capacitance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a fully integrated, all-digital, 125-MHz inductive buck voltage regulation IC in 130-nM CMOS.
the design of an all-digital fully integrated inductive voltage regulator (IVR) in 130-nM CMOS.
the design of a high-efficiency, low-cost, high-performance inductive buck regulator for use in high-performance computing systems, such as data centers, supercomputers, and mobile devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed design demonstrates a 250-MHz multi-sampled digital compensation with a lightweight auto-tuner and adaptive discontinuous mode control in an all-digital architecture to achieve a 71% peak efficiency and a 2-9V/$mu s$ output slew during large-reference transient.
the proposed IVR demonstrates the highest efficiency, highest slew rate, highest bandwidth, and lowest power consumption for a fully integrated inductive IVR in the literature.
the proposed IVR demonstrates a peak efficiency 71% at 1.5 A and a 3.3-V/ $\mu $ s output slew during large transient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IVR is able to achieve a 2.5-V output voltage at a 2.2-mA load current with a 2.8-V supply and a 125-MHz switching frequency.
the IVR is a fully integrated inductor-based regulator with an adaptive digital controller that can be easily tuned and integrated in a digital process node.
the presented architecture and design techniques enable the design of fully integrated inductive regulators for high-frequency operation in advanced digital process nodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fully integrated inductive VRM can be realized in digital process nodes without compromising performance.

an all-digital fully integrated inductive regulator can be implemented in a digital process with a high level of integration, and the digital architecture enables the use of a multi-sampled compensator and a fast and lightweight auto tuner, which significantly improve the transient performance of the regulator.
an all-digital IVR can be integrated in a digital process with a high level of performance, and that a lightweight auto-tuner is a promising approach to improve the robustness of IVRs.
